No var() anywhere uses them, and no element on any measured page paints them. They are what remains of the 2026-09-10 washes and the 2026-09-11 'more opaque red and blue' held word, both retired on 2026-09-11 according to the color contract. They are not counted and not folded: they are deleted, so /palette/ stops printing them as if they were colors of the site. --halo-shani rgba(157,67,85,.75) and --halo-tekhelet rgba(52,100,154,.75) are not grounds. They are the red and blue regulars at 75%, used as a text glow, and are read only under :root[data-accent="halo"], which nothing in the site sets. They count as the regulars and stay (they could also go together with their three dormant rules at zone.html ~352-356). No chip, shadow or border-wash in the site is red or blue: the reading's license chip is gold (--chip-line) and the shadows are brown. Every ground a red or blue word stands on belongs to linen. Measured contrast of the KEPT inks on those linen grounds: (1) Bare linen #ebdec3: red 4.68, blue 4.59, red dim 3.06, blue dim 2.56. (2) Card or rail #efe4cd/#ecdfc5: red 4.94/4.73, blue 4.85/4.64. (3) The word cell (rgba(74,48,8,.06) on linen, about rgb(225,212,184)): red 4.25, blue 4.17, blue dim + 2.32. (4) The run's tie (.08 more, about rgb(213,199,170)): red 3.74, blue 3.66. (5) The pressed linen #dccbaa: red 3.91, blue 3.83, blue dim 2.14. (6) Parchment #e8d9bc: red 4.48, red dim rail 2.93. (7) The door shelf card rgb(225,211,179): red 4.21, blue 4.12. All of these numbers were the same before the fold. The steer asks that a family's text read at 4.5:1 on linen AND on the word cell. In the word cell, NEITHER regular reaches 4.5:1 today (red 4.25 at 21px, blue 4.17 at 10.6px). The only red or blue that did was the bold blue being folded away (5.54). So that floor depends on the cell's linen, not on red or blue. For the same reason, red's and blue's running text cannot move to the dim (dims are 2.8:1 and 2.3:1 in the cell). In these two families the words stay in the regular and the dim stays on marks.
distinctions_lost: A pressed reading vs a reading at rest, on the reader's card and the door's card: before, the pressed one had a deeper blue, bold letters, a doubled gold border and darker linen. After, it keeps the bold letters, doubled gold border and darker linen, and loses only the deeper blue. It is still clearly pressed, because three cues remain and color was never the only one. The shots show the difference is slight. This matters only for contrast, which drops from 5.10:1 to 3.83:1 (see fold).
The pressed reading on the card vs the open word's reading on the line: these used to be two different blues, and now they are one. This is a gain in uniformity, not a loss.
On the door's word card, pressed pill vs resting pills: the resting pills there are purple (--muted), so hue still separates them. Nothing is lost.

The + between a reading's pieces vs the + inside a reading's own words ('and + the + earth'): KEPT apart, dim vs regular. If the + were folded into the regular blue, this distinction would be lost (see line-he-alt-plus-regular.png and pressed-and-plus-before-after.png). That is why the + stays dim even though it measures 2.32:1 in the word cell, under the 3:1 a mark needs. That shortfall is not caused by the fold. If 3:1 must hold for the +, the only kept blue that clears it is the regular, and then only spacing tells the two kinds of + apart.
Red: nothing is lost. Red was already exactly two shades, and the fold moves no red.

Titles vs running text in red and blue: there is no color split here, and there has been none since 2026-10-02 ('no title has a color of its own'). The steer's 'titles regular, text dim' cannot apply to these two families with existing values, because neither dim can carry a word (red dim 3.06:1, blue dim 2.56:1 on linen). Hebrew titles and Hebrew text, attested English names and readings all stay in the regular.

grounds: I chose these three linens: the ground (#ebdec3, and yes, the page ground is one of the three), the cell (the --cell-wash glaze on the ground, about #e1d4b8), and the pressed linen (#dccbaa). Rule for see-through washes: a wash counts as the color it lays down on the ground under it. A veil of the ground at any strength (the floating bar at 94%, the rail at 55%) is the ground. A glaze on the ground is the cell. No glaze may stack on another glaze or on the pressed linen, because that would make a fourth linen. For that reason the blob and the overlay band, which both sit inside a cell, become the opaque pressed linen and not a second glaze. Anything sticky that has to hide text scrolling under it (.c-mark-slot .lab, #hud .d-foot) uses the opaque ground. Chips are grounds: a chip is a small cell that holds text, so the zone's purple-gray chip tint and the door's brown chip tint both fold to the cell. Shadows are not grounds. --shadow-pop/--shadow-card/--shadow-hud rgba(96,80,48,.20-.32) and the door's scrim --shade rgba(96,80,48,.35) are depth under a floating card, never a surface anything is written on, so they stay as one shadow color. The weave is thread, not ground, and stays: the SVG noise on body and the card's rgba(110,84,46,.035/.03) lines (the owner, 2026-10-03: "id also add woven to huds"). I checked this by walking every element's painted background on Genesis with a card open, Amos with its commentary and index open, and the door.
